finding: mineocclude.probes.splits.validate_fold_manifest rejects the real, hash-verified, production ten_pilot_frame_fold_manifest.json with GroupedSplitError('Fold memberships differ from the deterministic seeded assignment.'). This is not a data-corruption or hash problem -- every input the check depends on (config_hash, analysis_config_version, fold_schema_version, n_splits, seed, per-layout row counts) matches exactly between the real manifest and D's own frozen configuration. The check fails because D's own _assign_validated_rows reproduction genuinely computes a different fold-to-layout assignment than what Person B's real production manifest declares.
recommended_next_step: Escalate to whoever owns mineocclude/probes/splits.py's fold-assignment algorithm (likely Person B, per that module's own docstring 'Deterministic layout-grouped fold assignment for Person B analyses') to reconcile _assign_validated_rows against the real algorithm Person B's production pipeline actually used, then re-run this exact dry run (build_all_trajectory_contexts against the real materialized fold manifest) to confirm agreement before any real baseline execution is authorized.
root_cause_characterization: _assign_validated_rows sorts layouts by (-row_count, tie_breaker(seed, layout_id)) and then greedily assigns each, in that order, to the currently-least-loaded fold (ties on load broken by lowest fold index). The seed-dependent tie_breaker only ever changes the outcome when two layouts share the exact same row count. All five real layout counts here are strictly distinct (409 > 387 > 335 > 292 > 272), so the tie_breaker never engages and the algorithm degenerates to a fixed, seed-invariant rank order (confirmed directly: three different seed values, including the real one, all produce the identical {layout_00:0, layout_01:1, layout_02:2, layout_03:3, layout_04:4} assignment). Person B's real production assignment is a non-trivial permutation of that rank order ({1,2,4,0,3}), meaning Person B's actual real fold-assignment procedure is genuinely seed-sensitive in a way this shared reproduction algorithm structurally cannot be whenever counts are distinct -- the common case, not an edge case.
